📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Hunger Games franchise is welcoming a new installment, Sunrise on the Reaping, the sixth film adaptation of Suzanne Collins’s best-selling dystopian saga.

Releasing on November 20, the film boasts a star-studded cast of about 33 actors and counting, poised to bring a blend of familiar names and upcoming faces to the world of Panem.

Ahead of the film, we’re reacquainting ourselves with beloved characters from the original trilogy, like Effie Trinket (Elle Fanning), Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin), Beetee (Kelvin Harrison Jr.), and Wiress (Maya Hawke). Even the completely upcoming characters, like Maysilee Donner and Lenore Dove, have family ties to well-known characters in the franchise.

In a recent development, based on Collins’s second prequel novel, Sunrise on the Reaping delves into the brutal 50th Hunger Games, spotlighting a young Haymitch Abernathy 24 years before he became Katniss and Peeta’s mentor. We, as readers, thought we knew a detailed account of the second Quarter Quell from Mockingjay, but as we learn in the Sunrise on the Reaping novel, much of what we learned was manipulated by the Capitol to be used as propaganda.

This much is still true: With twice the tributes, the 50th Hunger Games doubles the bloodshed, trauma, and size of the cast. To prepare for the inevitably heart-wrenching film, get to know the extensive cast.

Joseph Zada is a 21-year-old Australian actor best known for playing Johnny Sinclair in the television series We Were Liars and Cal Trask in East of Eden.

Sources indicate that zada demonstrates a very different side of Woody Harrelson’s character, before the biting sarcasm and heavy drinking. In the newly introduced film, we follow 16-year-old Haymitch’s harrowing journey through the 50th Hunger Games and, arguably, a more distressing journey after victory. We knew Zada was perfect for the role when he discussed re-creating Harrelson’s Mockingjay Part 2 red-carpet pajama moment.

Zada’s Instagram is @josephzada.

Elle Fanning is a 28-year-old American actress best known for her roles as Aurora in Maleficent, Syvie Russo in A Complete Unknown, and Catherine in The Great, as well as being half of an iconic sister duo with Dakota Fanning.

While Trinket is only a side character in Sunrise on the Reaping, her casting was one of the most highly anticipated, with fans almost unanimously agreeing that Fanning was the only correct choice to reprise Elizabeth Banks’s character. In Sunrise on the Reaping, Trinket is a young member of the Capitol styling and beauty team for District 12.

Fanning’s Instagram is @ellefanning.

It has been revealed that it’s possible that Suzanne Collins got tired of the endless Coriolanus Snow thirst edits on TikTok and went ahead and cast Voldemort. No, really, 63-year-old English actor Ralph Fiennes is best known for his role as Voldemort in the Harry Potter film series.

Industry observers note that fiennes plays President Snow, a younger version of the late Donald Sutherland’s character in the original trilogy and an older version of Tom Blythe’s character in The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. President Snow reaches his peak level of viciousness in Sunrise on the Reaping, and Fiennes is the perfect vessel to carry out Snow’s evil looks.

In a recent development, kieran Culkin is a 44-year-old actor best known for his roles in A Real Pain and Succession. Despite recently winning an Oscar, Emmy, Golden Globe, and SAG Award, his brother Macaulay still has him beat in household name recognition for his childhood role in Home Alone. Reprising Stanley Tucci's role as Hunger Games host Caesar Flickerman may change that.

Jesse Plemons is a 38-year-old actor best known for his roles in Friday Night Lights and Breaking Bad (and for being married to Kirsten Dunst). In another impeccable casting choice, Plemons also played the son of the original Plutarch (the late Philip Seymour Hoffman) in The Master (2012).

Industry observers note that in both Sunrise on the Reaping and the original trilogy, Plutarch Heavensbee is an old-money Capitol citizen whose morally gray philosophies make him one of the franchise’s most fascinating characters. In the newly introduced film, we see him as a young, ambitious cameraman, years before he became head gamemaker.

In a recent development, lili Taylor is a 59-year-old American actress and author best known for her roles in Mystic Pizza and The Conjuring. She has the perfect sweet smile to play Mags Flanagan, the victor of the 11th Hunger Games from District 4.

Mags, previously played by the late Lynn Cohen, was introduced in Catching Fire when she volunteered to take Annie Cresta's place in the 75th Hunger Games. In Sunrise on the Reaping, Mags acts as District 12's mentor, as they have no surviving winners of their own.

Taylor’s Instagram is @lilittaylor.

Maya Hawke is the 28-year-old daughter of Uma Thurman and Ethan Hawke, best known for her roles as Robin in Stranger Things and Anxiety in Inside Out 2.

Recent findings suggest that she plays Wiress, the District 3 victor fresh out of the 49th Hunger Games. Amanda Plummer played the character in Catching Fire, when she was reaped with Beetee as the 75th Hunger Games District 3 tributes.

Hawke's Instagram is @maya_hawke.

Kelvin Harrison Jr. is a 32-year-old actor who previously played the son of the original Beetee (Jeffrey Wright) in Monsters (2018).

Sources indicate that as the Hunger Games fan account Panem Propaganda mentioned, “If I had a nickel for every time a Sunrise on the Reaping cast member played the son of their older Hunger Games counterpart in a completely unrelated movie, I’d have two nickels. Which isn’t a lot, but it’s weird that it happened twice,” referring to the castings of Beetee and Plutarch.

According to recent reports, beetee was the winner of the 34th Hunger Games from District 3 who was reaped for the 75th Hunger Games in Catching Fire. The fresh film delves into his heartbreaking backstory, involving the fate of his son, Ampert, as well as his secret blueprint with Haymitch to disrupt the games.

Harrison's Instagram is @kelvinharrjr.

Industry observers note that iris Apatow is a 24-year-old actress who previously appeared in This Is 40, The Bubble, and Knocked Up. She is the daughter of actress Leslie Mann and producer Judd Apatow, the sister of Euphoria star Maude Apatow, and the girlfriend of White Lotus star Sam Nivola. She plays Proserpina Trinket, Effie’s younger sister and member of the District 12 prep team.

Recent findings suggest that edvin Ryding is a 23-year-old Swedish actor who previously appeared in 28 Years Later and Young Royals. He plays Vitus, Proserpina’s friend and sidekick on the District 12 prep team.

His Instagram is @edvinrydings.

Sources indicate that whitney Peak is a 23-year-old Ugandan-Canadian actress best known for her role as Zoya in the 2021 Gossip Girl reboot. She plays Lenore Dove, the Covey singer and love of Haymitch's life.

According to recent reports, though her character is unique to Sunrise on the Reaping, Lenore Dove is rumored to be the daughter of either Maude Ivory or Lucy Gray Baird. Fans can’t help but notice the resemblance between Peak and Rachel Zegler.

Peak's Instagram is @whitneypeak.

McKenna Grace is a 20-year-old actress best known for her roles in The Handmaid's Tale, Ghostbusters: Afterlife, and Young Sheldon. While young, she has been acting since she was five, and she has had at least 34 film and television roles.

She plays Maysilee Donner, the spoiled mean girl who turns into a star when she is reaped for the 50th Hunger Games. She has a twin sister, Merrilee (whose daughter later gifts Katniss the Mockingjay pin), and is friends with Asterid March, Katniss's mother. She allies herself with Haymitch during the game, and the two share a sibling-like bond.

Grace's Instagram is @mckennagraceful.

Ben Wang is a 29-year-old actor best known for his roles in Karate Kid: Legends and American Born Chinese.

He plays Wyatt Callow, Haymitch's fellow District 12 boy tribute. The Callow family runs the gambling scene in District 12, placing bets on the Hunger Games tributes each year.

Wang’s Instagram is @definitelynotbenwang.

Glenn Close is a 79-year-old Tony, Emmy, and Golden Globe winner best known for her roles in Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, and The Deliverance.

She plays Drusilla Sickle, the District 12 tributes’ escort. Drusilla is known for her many cosmetic surgeries that poorly attempt to disguise her age. She and Maysilee are the biggest divas in Panem, and their personalities clash disastrously.

Close’s Instagram is @glennclose.

Billy Porter is a 57-year-old Emmy, Tony, and Grammy Award–winning actor, singer, composer, director, and playwright.

He plays Magno Stift, the incompetent stylist for the District 12 tributes. His personal style involves wearing a plethora of live reptiles, and his hobbies include licking frogs for the psychedelic effects.

Porter’s Instagram is @theebillyporter.

Molly McCann is a young Irish actress who previously appeared in Bad Sisters, Herself, and Rosie. She plays Louella McCoy, a young girl from District 12 who Haymitch views as a little sister and nicknamed “Sweetheart.” Fans were quick to notice McCann's resemblance to Katniss (Jennifer Laurence), the only other character who Haymitch refers to as Sweetheart.

McCann’s Instagram is @mollymccannactress.

Iona Bell is a young English actress who plays Louella’s uncanny lookalike, Lou Lou.

Her Instagram is @iona_bell_official_actor.

Sources indicate that kara Tointon is a 43-year-old English actress who previously appeared in EastEnders, The Teacher, and Too Good to Be True. She plays Willamae Abernathy, Haymitch's mother.

Her Instagram is @kara_tointon.

How’d they get home? Is there really a supernatural force controlling them, in the wilderness and in New Jersey? Will anyone survive? What happened to Melissa’s hat? Follow this Yellowjackets season 4 schedule so you don’t miss a single second.

We’re going back to the wilderness. We’re going back to the equally chaotic present-day timeline. And since we now get to see the immediate aftermath of the young Yellowjackets’ return to civilization and processed food... we’re also going back to high school. The fourth season has also added a ton of upcoming cast members, including Molly Ringwald, Devon Sawa, June Squibb, Ken Marino, Eric Stoltz, and Dulé Hill.

The first episode premieres November 20, 2026 on streaming, and then subsequently will air on cable November 22, 2026.

Yellowjackets is a Showtime show, which means you can stream it on Paramount+ and then later watch it on the Showtime channel.

There are ten episodes in the final season of Yellowackets. There have been ten episodes every season except season 2... unless you count that totally real, but still totally unseen, secret unreleased episode.

Industry observers note that the holiday season is in full swing, with many halls and houses already decked to impress in garland and fairy lights. But as you wrap gifts, prepare to host, and begin marathoning holiday movies, it can feel like the joyous season is coming to an end much too soon. We can't blame you if you're still wanting more from this merry time of year, and we've come up with a solution. There are plenty of beautiful Christmas towns across the country to fill your heart with peace, joy, and nostalgia—you just have to know where to look.

Industry observers note that these towns are more than just beautifully decorated—they’re truly immersive, offering experiences from Santa-themed bike rides to orchestrated light indicates and winter bar crawls. Below, we've rounded up the 27 most charming Christmas towns from all over the country, so no matter where you live, you'll be close enough to find a bit of extra cheer this year.

Additional copy by Alyssa Khan.

This picturesque mountain town serves as the perfect holiday backdrop for more reasons than just the ever-present blanket of fluffy white snow. Each year, the valley is transformed into a Christmas town with seasonal theatrical performances, Gunnison’s Night of Lights, a tree lighting ceremony, and even an ice sculpting event.

According to recent reports, ever since the formation of this city on Christmas Eve in 1741, Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, has been rooted in the holiday spirit. From Christmas markets to historical tours to horse-drawn carriage rides, there's no doubt this town won't feel magical. And make sure to stop by the historic Sayre Mansion, pictured here, to check out their elegant holiday decor.

According to recent reports, annapolis is known as one of the best cities during the holiday season thanks to its winter weather and historic downtown. If you're lucky enough to visit this Christmas town, make sure you spend time bargain shopping until midnight, checking out the spectacular light display in Sandy Point State Park, and viewing the Yacht Club Light Parade.

Industry observers note that chicago is exceptionally beautiful during the Christmas time. From the seemingly endless strings of lights to the Christkindlmarket, which is free to enter and so charming, the Windy City has many offerings during the holiday season, making it one of the best Christmas towns to visit. Plus, you don't want to miss ice skating or any Christmas-themed museum exhibits.

If you want to do something Christmas-y almost every single day of December, then Newport, Rhode Island, might just be the place to go. To create the perfect coastal Christmas, this town offers a month-long celebration that's been going strong for 54 years. From holiday bike rides to Medieval festivals to winter afternoon teas, there's so much to do in this Christmas town.

In a recent development, you'll feel as if you've traveled back to Charles Dickens's time when you walk through Franklin's historic Christmas festival. Characters from A Christmas Carol and Oliver Twist come to life throughout the weekend-long festivities. Roam the Victorian Village and try Victorian-era Christmas treats like sugar plums while listening to carolers.

A classic ski town, Park City offers Christmas markets, festive decorations, and a Christmas Eve parade lit by torches—plus spectacular views of the mountains are around every corner.

Industry observers note that in the heart of Virginia horse country, you'll find one of the most festive Christmas towns. Cheer on the town's hunting hounds while sipping hard cider and wander the streets in search of vintage Christmas ornaments.

In a recent development, during Kennebunkport's annual Christmas Prelude, the town puts on a very New England celebration: You can watch Santa Claus arrive by lobster boat, go on seashore holiday trolley rides, and enjoy wine tastings and lobster bakes. Not to mention, the town is covered in Christmas lights and garlands that make it the perfect festive photo backdrop.

Industry observers note that for a dreamy and unique experience, head to Santa Fe. One of the most anticipated celebrations is the Canyon Road Farolito Walk, which is when thousands of farolitos—luminaries made of paper bags, sand, and tea candles—cast a glow on the gardens and old buildings that line the road. You also can get your white Christmas fix by visiting Ski Santa Fe.

According to recent reports, as one of the oldest towns in the country, Portsmouth is a charming New England destination that celebrates the holidays with a Vintage Christmas Celebration. Visit the historic village of Strawberry Banke or wander around the charming shopping districts in this historic Christmas town.

Recent findings suggest that get a Hallmark movie feel while experiencing a taste of Denmark in California's Solvang village, located in Santa Ynez Valley wine country. The destination hosts Julefest, a month-long holiday celebration with live entertainment, a parade, and a night market.

Koziar's Christmas Village in Bernville is one of the top attractions in Pennsylvania. With more than a million lights adorning buildings, barns, and the landscape—and a reflective lake that doubles the beauty—it's hard to beat the town's display.

According to recent reports, this Bavarian-style village is charming any time of year! December festivities include a display of Santa costumes from all around the world, a gingerbread house competition, carolers, and plenty of photo ops.

Recent findings suggest that of course, New York City isn't a small Christmas town, but it is extra magical during the holidays. From the massive tree at Rockefeller Center to the various Christmas markets in the city parks with ice skating, shops, and more, you can't beat the Substantial Apple's holiday spirit.

In a recent development, nicknamed the Lighted Poinsettia Capital of Texas, this town brings major holiday spirit every year. Visit during December when the lighted trail in Comanche Trail Park is aglow all month long. Check out Hotel Settles for its elegant Art Deco lodging.

It has been revealed that during the holiday season, each home in Historic Williamsburg lights one candle, a tradition that dates back to the Revolutionary War era. The cobblestone streets and colonial holiday traditions such as caroling by torchlight make this destination a must, especially for history buffs.

This Christmas town stays decked out year-round, so if you're craving holiday spirit in July, you'll still find candy-cane posts, boughs of holly, and a Santa Claus house with live reindeer!

Christmas without the cold? We've got you covered! In addition to abundant sunshine and festive holiday decor, you'll also have plenty of history to explore in St. Augustine, America's oldest city.

It has been revealed that want to take a ride on the Polar Express? Visit Durango during the holidays. The historic mining town offers a Polar Express–inspired trip that your kiddos will flip over.

Safe Word: The Best Jewelry Introduces of November 2026

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2610 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Safe Word is a series highlighting the latest trends in the jewelry market, keeping you up to date on all things that sparkle and shine.
  • November’s jewelry launches are looking both backward and forward, with designers revisiting their roots, reworking archival ideas, and stepping into entirely new territory.
  • Quentin Jones is taking her art off the wall and onto the body with “Nocturne,” the first jewelry collection from House of Quentin Jones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Safe Word is a series highlighting the latest trends in the jewelry market, keeping you up to date on all things that sparkle and shine.

November’s jewelry launches are looking both backward and forward, with designers revisiting their roots, reworking archival ideas, and stepping into entirely new territory. First up, Quentin Jones is taking her surrealist art off the wall and onto the body with “Nocturne,” her first jewelry collection; Pomellato reaches back to 1997 to revive “Moneta Orientale” as a colorful modern talisman; David Yurman celebrates the magic of a New York holiday with Michael B. Jordan, Yerin Ha, and Inde Navarrette; Vhernier revisits its iconic “Trottola” design with new proportions and contrasting materials; Di Volpe reinterprets the classic tennis bracelet with customizable gemstones in “DiSegno”; Brent Neale transforms the classic bow into sculptural fine jewelry with “Wrap It Up”; and Kendra Scott launches the new “Kendra Scott Collection,” reimagining her signature Spike motif as a personal talisman. From archival revivals and meaningful motifs to innovative designs and new creative directions, November’s launches prove that sometimes the best way forward starts with looking back. For the rest of the month, we’ve got you covered on all the jewelry-related happenings worth knowing about.

Quentin Jones Turns Her Art Into Jewelry.

Quentin Jones is taking her art off the wall and onto the body with “Nocturne,” the first jewelry collection from House of Quentin Jones. Following the multidisciplinary artist’s debut of surrealist ceramics and tapestries last year, the upcoming collection transforms recurring gestures and symbols from her work into sculptural collars, cuffs, armbands, pendants, chains, and earrings. Eyes, hands, stars, moons, tears, and knots take shape in silver and gold vermeil alongside freshwater pearls, onyx, opals, jade, glass, and silk tassels, giving the pieces a dreamlike, talismanic quality. Beginning as drawings and hand collages in Jones’s Brooklyn studio, each design carries her surrealist visual language into wearable form, further blurring the line between art, design, and fashion.

Piotrek Panszczyk Makes His Debut at Ippolita.

Recent findings suggest that ippolita is entering a new chapter under creative director Piotrek Panszczyk, who makes his debut at the house with “Ancient Bohemia,” a collection inspired by its archives and the organic forms of nature. Taking a sculptural approach to jewelry, Panszczyk reimagines familiar signatures with an emphasis on texture, craftsmanship, and unconventional layering. The house’s iconic Wavy Disk becomes the Wavy Coin, featuring Hippolyta, Queen of the Amazons and the brand’s namesake, as a symbol of feminine strength. Elsewhere, hand-sculpted Stardust pavé is set entirely with diamonds, pearls make their first appearance, and lightweight, hand-hammered silver Roma links offer multiple ways to wear, from necklaces to belts. Lapis lazuli, mother-of-pearl, and quartz introduce color through Ippolita’s signature layered doublets and triplets, mixed rather than matched for an eclectic finish. The result is a fresh interpretation of the house’s heritage that feels both ancient and distinctly modern.

Jade Trau and Luis Morais Combine Gemstones and Diamonds.

It has been revealed that jade Trau and Luis Morais are joining forces for a limited-edition collection that brings together their different approaches to fine jewelry. Comprised of 16 one-of-a-kind pieces, including 12 bracelets and four necklaces, the collaboration pairs Morais’s colorful gemstone beads with Trau’s signature 18-karat gold and diamond elements. The designs feature a vibrant mix of stones, from chrysoprase and amazonite to lapis lazuli, turquoise, carnelian, and tiger’s-eye, accented by recognizable Jade Trau details like the Frankie rondelle, Sophisticate station, and Georgie diamond lock. Designed with everyday wear in mind, the bracelets lend themselves to layering, while the necklaces incorporate Trau’s diamond-set closures. The result is a playful meeting of color and craftsmanship that brings a fresh perspective to both designers’ signatures.

Lagos Looks to the Stars With Its Latest Collection.

It has been revealed that lagos references the night sky in its latest fine jewelry collection, taking inspiration from the North Star and its centuries-old symbolism of guidance and possibility. Designed to celebrate milestones, newly introduced beginnings, and meaningful connections, the “North Star” collection features sculptural star motifs crafted in 18-karat gold and illuminated by natural diamonds. Cascading silhouettes and light-catching details bring a sense of movement to the celestial designs, balancing statement-making shapes with delicate craftsmanship. Both symbolic and sophisticated, the assortment offers a modern interpretation of a timeless emblem, making each piece a reminder of the people and moments that guide us.

Kendra Scott Debuts an Eponymous Collection.

In a recent development, kendra Scott is offering a more personal look into her design world with the launch of the “Kendra Scott Collection,” a newly introduced line spanning fashion and fine jewelry. Its first edition, “The Spike,” revisits a silhouette the designer has worn throughout her career as a personal symbol of strength, confidence, and conviction. Inspired by nature and the radiance of the night sky, the collection translates the pointed motif into sculptural necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and charms, balancing bold proportions with intricate craftsmanship. Fashion jewelry incorporates tiger’s eye, malachite, and turquoise, while fine jewelry introduces lab-grown diamonds, pavé detailing, labradorite, and lapis. From statement-making links to delicate diamond charms, the collection offers a new interpretation of Scott’s longtime signature, inviting wearers to make the symbol their own.

Alison Lou’s ‘New Wave’ Collection Experiments With New Materials.

Industry observers note that alison Lou is entering a latest chapter with “New Wave,” a fine jewelry collection that introduces unexpected materials and a fresh approach to the designer’s signature playful aesthetic. Exploring the relationship between movement and form, the collection pairs lightweight titanium and ceramic with lab-grown diamonds, creating fluid, sculptural silhouettes that curve and catch the light. Available in Fig and Denim Blue colorways, the designs include wavy rings, diamond-accented signets, delicate thread necklaces, and statement drop earrings. With its unconventional materials and easy-to-wear designs, “New Wave” brings a new sense of movement to Alison Lou’s everyday jewelry.

Jenny Bird and Emese Gormley Partner on the Anyu Ring.

Recent findings suggest that jenny Bird is expanding her JB FINE collection with a latest collaboration featuring lifestyle creator and Lipstick on the Rim podcast host Emese Gormley. Named in honor of Gormley’s mother, the Anyu Ring offers a personal take on the classic signet, featuring three lab-grown baguette diamonds set in 14-karat yellow or white gold. The understated design combines the timeless appeal of a signet ring with a sentimental tribute to family, bringing a new perspective to Bird’s growing fine jewelry offering. Available exclusively on Jenny Bird’s website, the collaboration makes a case for jewelry that feels as meaningful as it looks.

Pomellato Revives Its 1997 Moneta Orientale Pendant as a Colorful Talisman.

Pomellato is looking to its archives for its latest good-luck charm. For the newest chapter of “Memorie d’Archivio,” the maison revives Moneta Orientale, a 1997 pendant inspired by the ancient symbolism of a circle surrounding a square, representing the harmony between heaven and earth. Made in 33 stone-and-pavé combinations, the design pairs colorful hard stones including black jade, amazonite, sodalite, rhodochrosite, and labradorite with Pomellato’s signature irregular pavé of diamonds, sapphires, rubies, and more. Offered in two proportions, each pendant transforms the archival motif into a modern talisman for prosperity and protection.

Bibi van der Velden Makes Her High Jewelry Debut With ‘Eclipse’.

In a recent development, bibi van der Velden is entering a new era with “Eclipse,” the designer’s first high jewelry collection and most refined exploration of diamonds to date. Inspired by the fleeting moment when light gives way to darkness, the collection includes two six-piece suites: one in white diamonds and another defined by an ombré of diamonds into gray spinels deepening into black. Van der Velden’s signature alligator motif is abstracted into fluid, sculptural silhouettes, with scales engraved into the white gold on the reverse of each piece. “With Eclipse, I wanted to take those familiar elements and transform them into something more abstract and sculptural,” she says. “It’s a collection about transformation, which has always been at the heart of my work.”.

Aflalo and Leandra Medine Cohen Turn Everyday Indulgences Into Fine Jewelry.

Aflalo is finding the humor in our obsession with wellness with “The Vanities,” a upcoming two-piece fine jewelry capsule designed exclusively by Leandra Medine Cohen. Playing with the contradiction between longevity and life’s little indulgences, the collection transforms two unlikely everyday accessories into precious objects. The Memento Mori is a 14-karat yellow gold cigar band set with more than four carats of diamonds, designed to slip over an Oura Ring, while The Libertine is a sterling silver pendant case adorned with diamonds and a wild-haired woman outlined in gold, designed to hold nicotine pouches or other small essentials. Equal parts extravagant and irreverent, the collection makes a playful case for enjoying life’s pleasures without sacrificing personal style.

Julia Berolzheimer’s Hart Jewelry Collection Draws on Childhood Memories.

Hart is teaming up with Julia Berolzheimer for a new jewelry collection that celebrates the art of the stack. Inspired by Berolzheimer’s childhood memories of her grandmother’s California ranch and her collection of Art Deco minaudières, the collaboration brings together whimsical charms, colorful gemstones, and meaningful talismans designed to be mixed, layered, and restyled. Botanical motifs take shape in Tree of Life coins, daisies, bees, and fruit-inspired charms, while carnelian, turquoise, and pink opal add playful pops of color. One standout is the Perfume Vesta Case, a modern interpretation of a Victorian-era accessory that can hold a sample-sized fragrance and hang alongside other charms. With interchangeable chains, cords, and pendants, the collection makes a case for jewelry that feels just as personal as the memories behind it.

David Yurman Captures the Magic of a New York Holiday.

Industry observers note that david Yurman is celebrating the magic of the holidays in Newly introduced York City with a new campaign featuring global brand ambassador Michael B. Jordan alongside actresses Yerin Ha and Inde Navarrette. Set against a snow-covered Washington Square Park, the campaign captures a series of quintessential New York moments, from Jordan and Ha facing off in a spirited card game to Navarrette hailing a cab in search of the perfect holiday gift. Throughout the campaign, the cast wears some of the house’s most recognizable designs, including 18-karat gold Cable bracelets and pieces from the “Starburst” and “Armory” collections. Directed by Bradford Young and photographed by Drew Vickers, the campaign brings together the spirit of the city, the joy of togetherness, and the timeless appeal of David Yurman’s jewelry.

Vhernier Reintroduces Its Iconic ‘Trottola’ Design With Latest Proportions.

It has been revealed that vhernier is revisiting one of its most recognizable designs with a fresh interpretation of “Trottola,” the sculptural collection originally introduced in 2003. Inspired by the continuous motion of a spinning top, the latest designs play with proportions, contrasting materials, and asymmetrical shapes across rings, bracelets, necklaces, and earrings. Polished rose gold meets glossy black jet, with select pieces featuring diamond pavé for an added contrast of light and dark. The collection also focuses on versatility, from rings designed for stacking to convertible earclips that can be worn as studs or dangling earrings. With its fluid forms and unexpected material combinations, “Trottola” brings a fresh perspective to Vhernier’s signature sculptural approach to jewelry.

Di Volpe Reinvents the Tennis Bracelet.

According to recent reports, di Volpe is rethinking the classic tennis bracelet with “DiSegno,” a upcoming customizable fine jewelry system designed to change with its wearer. Using concealed, patent-pending connections, individual cultured diamonds and gemstones, called Elements, can be removed, rearranged, or added by hand, allowing wearers to transform bracelets into necklaces or earrings without compromising the seamless look of traditional tennis jewelry. The collection introduces with 28 stone-and-cut combinations, including rubies, emeralds, sapphires, and diamonds, alongside a limited-edition collaboration with Lebanese artist Ali Cha’aban featuring five sculptural designs. With new cuts, colors, and artist collaborations planned for future releases, “DiSegno” makes the case for fine jewelry that’s never quite finished.

Brent Neale Riffs on the Bow in Fine Jewelry.

In a recent development, brent Neale is putting a bow on the holiday season with “Wrap It Up,” a upcoming fine jewelry collection that transforms the familiar ribbon motif into sculptural works of art. Drawing inspiration from Old Hollywood glamour and the femininity of the 1960s, the designer plays with the contrast between rigid precious metals and the soft movement of fabric, crafting bows that twist, curl, and unfurl in 18-karat gold and platinum. Colored gemstones sit nestled within the ribbon-like forms, while pavé diamonds accentuate every curve and fold. Equal parts playful and precious, the collection brings a little gift-wrapped glamour to the jewelry box.

Grace Winfrey’s ‘Poppy Fortuna’ Collection Reimagines Good-Luck Charms.

Grace Winfrey is bringing a little extra luck to the jewelry box with “Poppy Fortuna,” a fresh fine jewelry collection inspired by the natural beauty of the Italian landscape and symbols of good fortune. Scarlet poppies, sunflowers, bees, four-leaf clovers, horseshoes, and ladybugs come to life through vibrant gemstones and intricate pavé, creating miniature mosaics of color and texture. Highlights include a Lucky Bangle combining three good-luck charms, sculptural sunflower earrings with tiny ladybugs tucked into their petals, and layered charm necklaces designed to feel like modern keepsakes. Handcrafted in New York City, each piece transforms familiar symbols of prosperity, protection, and happiness into playful, colorful works of art.

Robinson Pelham Channels ’90s Glamour for Its Anniversary.

Industry observers note that robinson Pelham is closing out its 30th anniversary celebrations with “Suite 96,” a fresh campaign and collection launch inspired by the glamour of late-’90s London. Set inside a private suite at St. James’s Hotel & Club in Mayfair, the campaign considers jewelry the ultimate room service, with diamonds arriving on trays, gold spilling out of wardrobes, and plenty of pieces to layer before a night out. At the center is “Studio 30,” a four-piece anniversary collection featuring diamond necklaces and statement earrings, including the sculptural Via and Hira necklaces, cascading diamond drops, and the bold Solstice Supreme. Alongside the anniversary designs, the house introduces new collections and additions to existing favorites, from chunky gold links and graphic heart rings to colorful enamel and gemstone combinations. Together, the launches celebrate three decades of Robinson Pelham’s bold, playful approach to fine jewelry.

Le Vian and Jared Revive Georgian-Era Romance.

Le Vian is bringing a little old-world romance to Jared Jewelers with its latest exclusive “Georgian Chocolate & Nude Diamonds” collection. Inspired by the candlelit jewels of the Georgian era, when jewelry was designed to capture and reflect the warmth of natural light, the collection rethinks historic buttercup settings in polished Honey Gold, with eight rounded prongs framing each natural diamond. The designs pair Le Vian’s signature Chocolate and Nude Diamonds with warm gold detailing across solitaire rings, anniversary bands, tennis bracelets, necklaces, and earrings. Select styles introduce colorful gemstones including Chocolate Quartz, Green Apple Peridot, and Grape Amethyst, giving the vintage-inspired silhouettes a contemporary update. With its sculptural settings and warm-toned stones, the collection brings the romance of antique jewelry into the present.

Wempe’s ‘Au:thentic’ Celebrates the Art of Goldsmithing.

In a recent development, wempe’s new gender-inclusive fine jewelry collection, “Au:thentic,” puts craftsmanship front and center, finding inspiration in the foundational skills taught to aspiring goldsmiths. The collection takes its shape from the jump ring, one of the first techniques Patrick Sieroslawski learned as an apprentice more than 22 years ago, translating its form to necklaces, bracelets, rings, earrings, and pendants. Handcrafted at Wempe’s atelier in Germany, the pieces come in 18-karat yellow, white, and rose gold, with select styles set with diamonds. “Au:thentic” also marks the beginning of a multiyear rollout, with three additional chapters set to expand on its design language through twists, wraps, and interlocking links.

Sources indicate that the Traitors may be a game of deceit, but Victor Vollbrechthausen and Katie Fites’ flirtation? That was apparently very real.

As the first civilian-only season of The Traitors: New Blood came to a close, host Alan Cumming asked Katie, “Is there a possible date on the cards for you and Victor?”.

According to recent reports, she seemed tainted by the fact that Victor had banished her, jokingly saying, “No date for you,” until he kept the banter going and claimed that he “earned it” after finding out she was a Traitor. Now, the star-crossed Faithful and Traitor romance has seemingly made its way out of Alan’s Scottish castle.

During a joint postseason interview with Entertainment Weekly, Victor and Katie revealed they followed through on their aims and actually went on a first date.

In a recent development, “We have gone on that date. After incessant begging, let the kids back home know that persistence works,” Katie joked, before revealing that it was “great.”.

It has been revealed that “It was fun to get to know each other outside of her trying to murder me, me trying not to get murdered. It was nice to take a moment just for us,” Victor, who played as a Faithful while Katie was one of the season’s Traitors, told the outlet.

As for what their first date entailed? Well, there was certainly no discussion about their time on the show, since Victor banned any mention of it. And, honestly, who can blame him? After all, he was onto Katie’s strategy to potentially target him for murder.

Sources indicate that while her crush on Victor helped her game, Katie admitted that she genuinely enjoyed hanging out with him and even grew close to him throughout the season. She also revealed that she didn’t immediately kill Victor off because she wasn’t aware of his suspicions toward her—though he had been side-eyeing her earlier on than she realized.

The pair remained coy about whether they’ll keep their showmance going offscreen. When asked if they had plans to go on a second date, Victor shared, “Let’s see. Listen, man, it’s gonna... I don’t know. Getting that first one was an uphill battle, but I think there could be.”.

It has been revealed that “I think there could be,” Katie added. “But we’ll see. Gonna have to keep persisting.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Seasonal travel is exciting, but getting everyone from point A to point B can be a production—especially when babies and pets are involved. Between navigating crowded airports, packing the car with what feels like half your house, and keeping your four-legged family members calm amid all the chaos, there’s a ton to think about. And while you can’t control flight delays, holiday traffic, or the timing of a much-needed diaper change, having the right travel gear can make a world of difference.

According to recent reports, enter Nuna and Tavo, two brands that bring thoughtful design, innovative safety features, and a beautiful aesthetic to (often hectic) family travel. Nuna’s premium baby gear helps take some of the stress out of everything from airport security to car-seat installations, while Tavo focuses the same level of attention on the safety and comfort of travel essentials designed specifically for pets. Think lightweight strollers that fold with one hand (because your other one is probably occupied), car seats that don’t require an online tutorial to install, and comfortable carriers that give your furry companions a safe spot of their own.

Whether you’re flying across the country to visit the grandparents, packing up for a holiday road trip, or exploring a new destination together, these six Nuna and Tavo essentials, available at Bloomingdale’s, can help make the journey a little more joyful for everyone involved.

Industry observers note that given crowded security lines, blowouts at the worst possible moment, and the sheer amount of stuff you have to tote, a lightweight stroller is a genuine lifesaver at the airport. At just 16.3 pounds, the Nuna VIAA cabn is designed to meet IATA cabin-size standards when folded with the armbar removed—though you’ll still want to double-check your airline’s requirements. One-handed steering makes navigating crowded terminals easier (especially when you’re juggling a much-needed iced coffee), while a roomy storage basket holds up to 22 pounds of diaper bags, coats, backup outfits, bottles, snacks, and approximately 47 things to keep your baby entertained. It even comes with a carrier bag for when it’s time to board.

It has been revealed that this Nuna duo pairs the TRIV lx stroller, which folds with one hand and stands on its own, with the ultralight PIPA urbn infant car seat. And if you’ve ever broken a sweat or found yourself YouTubing car seat installation instructions for the 100th time, you’ll appreciate that this one clicks into place without a base, using its built-in pipaFIX rigid latch installation. Large rear wheels and all-wheel suspension pair with a spacious storage basket and handy tracking-device pocket to make the stroller ready for everyday outings.

Industry observers note that the Nuna SWIV’s standout feature is button-activated 360-degree rotation on all four wheels, allowing it to move sideways and pivot through tight spaces without the struggle of squeezing through crowded airport lines and store aisles that clearly weren’t designed with strollers in mind. A one-handed recline with three positions, including a near-flat option, makes adjustments easy, and the stroller is travel-system-ready with any Nuna PIPA series infant car seat, allowing you to move baby from the car to the stroller.

Sources indicate that the Tavo Crispin gives your pet a roomy, comfortable spot of their own, with mesh panels for ventilation and visibility so they can still keep eyes on their humans. It’s impact-tested and secures to your vehicle using lower anchors and a top tether, with a protective memory-foam guard for added peace of mind. And when the holiday travels are over, it collapses for easy storage without taking up precious space at home.

Recent findings suggest that this Tavo travel system might be your latest favorite on-the-road companion. The Maeve car seat attaches to the Roscoe Trek stroller frame, so you can go from the car to a festive outing without having to transfer your pup to a different carrier. All-terrain rear wheels and suspension make bumpy sidewalks easier to navigate, while one-touch brakes and a compact stroller fold come in handy when it’s time for a coffee stop or to load everything back into the car.

There’s a very particular type of heart-rate spike that comes with flying with a pet. You have to stand in the airline’s special-assistance line with your (probably nervous) dog or cat, only to finally reach the counter and hold your breath as the agent (and sometimes a supervisor) decides whether their carrier fulfills the rules. The Tavo Dupree II has a chic carry-on design that’s also crash-tested, complete with built-in vehicle connectors and a protective memory-foam guard. Mesh panels keep air circulating, while a trolley sleeve lets you slip it over your suitcase handle instead of carrying everything separately. You’ll still want to double-check your airline’s requirements before flying.

Industry observers note that for the kitchen’s centerpiece, designer Susan Ford of Bennett Hofford chose a La Cornue CornuFé range in Quintessential Teal. White-veined marble, creamy cabinetry, and golden hardware frame the deep blue hue, which continues across the lower cabinets to anchor the design.

The color also plays beautifully against the plush terra-cotta stools lining the island. Designer Chloe Legras of Boxwood Avenue, who designed the adjacent great room, selected the stools and other kitchen accents.

Recent findings suggest that beyond its color, the range features millwork in mixed metals, giving the traditional detail a futuristic edge and adding character to the small but bespoke space. A Parisian-style range hood with gold details completes the look.

If you’re looking to elevate your kitchen, take a cue from our Whole Home. This design is bold enough to impress the design-obsessed and practical enough for the bustle of everyday life.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nothing is simple in MobLand. Two seasons in, the plot has racked up more lines than Eddie put up his nose the night he stabbed Tommy Stevenson in season 1. Actually, that’s not strictly true. One thing is simple in MobLand: Eddie. He is a simpleton of truly Homeric (as in Simpson) proportions: a smarmy, sneering, simpering Freudian mess, channelled with gimlet-eyed precision by Anson Boon. All he wants is his God-given right to be respected.

According to recent reports, trouble is, when you’re an anti-Midas who turns everything he touches to shit, respect is a dish that never leaves the kitchen. Eddie is, in Kevin’s words in season 1, “a knifey little twerp.” That stabbing set the whole bloody saga in motion, so it’s only right that two seasons later we end with Eddie the Incompetent. Full circle, then, like a roundabout made of corpses.

According to recent reports, mobLand opened with Eddie turning a stabbing into a gang war, so it seems fitting that we end with Eddie turning an assassination into an own goal. But we’ll get to that.

It seems Conrad’s chickens are coming home to roost, and his marbles are jangling around his head like loose change. We open the episode with his card being declined at a petrol station. In frustration, he shoots the till boy dead. But he knows what it means.

According to recent reports, “We’re getting lifted,” he tells Maeve in the car. Police are raiding the entire business: bank accounts are frozen, warrants are out, and Tattersall is telling reporters the Harrigans have links to terror groups across the globe. The family convenes at a dingy old safe house out of town.

“We’re terrorists,” says Seraphina. “We’re looking at life in Guantánamo. It’s now or never.”.

According to recent reports, her blueprint has been bubbling for a while. She calls it Harrigan 2.0: going global.

In a recent development, remember the diplomatic suitcase of diamonds Seraphina collected from her billionaire stepdad Charlton in the last episode? It was meant to fund her and Bella’s takeover of the Harrigan operation. Now, it seems, Harry has it. He takes her aside to let her know he knows. “How did you know?” she asks, incredulous.

Then he claims the three words he says more than any others in MobLand: “It’s my job.”.

Inside the safe house, the family are all there, and everyone has a plan to pitch. Kevin wants to crawl back to Kat and hand over Conrad, Maeve, and Eddie. “Clean the house,” he growls to Harry, out of earshot of the others.

Conrad, meanwhile, isn’t sure what to do. “What are our options?” he asks Harry.

“We don’t have any,” comes the terse reply. “Either we run seven ways and it’s every man and woman for themselves, or we go back to Kat and try to strike some kind of deal.”.

Kevin proposes offering her 50 percent and first working out who’s a liability. “And right now I’m seeing a lot of liabilities. Right, Harry?”.

In a recent development, bella has had it up to ’ere with Kevin’s pusillanimity. “Oh, you nearly got to the end of a sentence without saying ‘Harry,’” she taunts. “I know he saved you from a bumming once but… Jesus.”.

According to recent reports, kevin pulls a pistol and fires, missing her ear by millimeters. Conrad draws. “Put the gun down, boy,” he hisses. Bella steps forward. “Go on then, big boy.”.

You could cut the tension with piano wire.

According to recent reports, “Fuck this, I’m getting us out of this mess,” notes Seraphina, defusing the standoff by fetching a fistful of diamonds from the car. “Fifteen Type IIa brilliants. North of ten million euros,” she tells Conrad, placing them in his hand.

The proposal: offer Kat a cut of the empire. “This time tomorrow we’re back in business.”.

Remember that glorious, long-winded speech Conrad gave in Spain about the good old days, how he came from nothing, and how Maeve has been his compass through the carnage of his life? “We were born outlaws and we’ll die outlaws,” he bellowed.

Well, now he knows the jig is up. Looking balefully at the floor, he grunts: “Do it.”.

In a recent development, so how will Harry play this? He slips out to his 4x4 and rings Kat. “At 5 p.m. I will meet your diplomatic courier. I will pass to said courier €10 million in untraceable diamonds. Upon authentication, I will give you the location of the Harrigan family.”.

Sources indicate that A double cross? It must be a ruse. He simply MUST have a blueprint… Then, hanging up, he mutters: “Fuck this, I’m done.”.

He returns to the family and lies: “Kat will take the ten million and 50 percent.” Too easy by half.

As Frankie put it two episodes ago: “Is that it? Unless you’ve got some brilliant looks, that is actually a bit shit. What are you up to, Harry?”.

Recent findings suggest that we’re more than halfway through and haven’t heard a peep from Frankie, our laconic, crocodilian villain. Ah, but here he is, getting the news of Harry’s volte-face from Tattersall. “How do we know it’s not a bluff?”.

Recent findings suggest that “He’s not stupid,” says Tattersall. “He knows when the game’s up.”.

It has been revealed that “Well, you know me,” leers Frankie. “I can’t resist a gamble.” Guns are grabbed from car boots, and off he pootles with a gaggle of tooled-up goons to send the Harrigans back to Hell.

Recent findings suggest that it’s all unfolding very promptly now, as denouements always should. Back at the safe house, Conrad is still seeing the dead, including the petrol station lad he just murdered. Maeve notes he’s been saying their names in his sleep.

According to recent reports, the old loon’s marbles are now departing his head like passengers from a cancelled flight. But there’s one thing that’ll straighten any man out: a black pearl of Maeve wisdom. “We’ve been stuck up tighter holes than Kat McAllister’s,” she reassures him. “But when you’re stuck up someone’s hole, there’s at least two ways out.”.

According to recent reports, quite so. And who better to lead the way than Harry? As ever, he picks the exit that leads straight back to where he came in. Unbeknownst to us, he has gone up Kat’s backside, rummaged about, and come out the other end holding her entire career. The “betrayal” was a ruse from the start.

So when Frankie’s goons arrive armed to the teeth, it’s a trap: flash grenades, smoke grenades, poison gas, and Zosia on the exit with a machine gun for anyone daft enough to run. “Oh, Harry,” concedes Frankie, before a mighty gunfight erupts and Harry tears through the house like Keyser Söze in a gas mask. “So this isn’t the beginning of a beautiful friendship,” smiles Frankie, choking in the corner. Harry shoots him in the knee.

Then Harry rings Kat. Those “untraceable” diamonds? Very traceable indeed, straight to a terrorist organization. He has bribed a low-ranking diplomatic courier to deliver them along with a “little present, just for you.”.

In a recent development, she opens the box, ashen-faced. It’s Donnie’s blue and rotting head. “This one you might find harder to justify,” he tells her.

“My family are gonna hunt you down and feed you your balls,” she spits.

Recent findings suggest that “Probably,” claims Harry. “But not before they feed you yours.”.

Industry observers note that checkmate, Kat. The black queen has no more squares to go.

But wait … Harry can offer her one square. “I can fix this,” he indicates.

In a recent development, here’s what she’s going to do. She’ll resign. She’ll kill the police investigation. The Harrigans’ accounts will reopen and they’ll come off the terror list.

Recent findings suggest that cut to a London corridor of power, where a faceless civil servant informs DS Kavanagh that “continuation of your terrorism financing line will interfere with an active joint intelligence operation between British and American security services. You will stand down at the close of business.”.

And so, full circle. Maeve is electrocuting Frankie’s balls with a car battery. Kevin is building bridges with Bella. Conrad is going madder by the day. And Eddie?

The Semtex he blackmailed Paul for was meant for Harry, at Maeve’s behest. In the hands of any other Harrigan, this would be a doddle. But not Eddie. Not the knifey little twerp, a man who could trip over his own foreskin in an empty car park.

According to recent reports, and he does. But first, the hints. Something strange has been going on with Jan all episode: the soppy Damien Rice soundtrack, the wistful dream sequences of the good times she shared with Harry. Her Harry. The one she fell for in the first place. She seems to have forgiven him. They’re even taking a family holiday.

In a recent development, but there’s one last stop before they go: Harrigan HQ, where Eddie is lying in wait. While Harry negotiates the terms of the holiday with Conrad, Gina and Jan stroll over to the lake. It’s Eddie’s moment, his chance to shine. He plants the Semtex in their car, hides around the corner, arms the bomb, finger hovering over the detonator … then a phone call.

By Finn McCool’s cobblers, it’s Kelly “Mad Dog” O’Connor, the lunatic son of the Medusa, whom Maeve sent Eddie to kill. “I’m coming for you,” growls the voice. “The Mad Dog is coming.”.

Gina, Jan and Harry return to the car. Only Jan gets in. In his quivering, fearful state, Eddie trips and drops the detonator.

Recent findings suggest that that’s Jan up in smoke, along with Harry’s plans for a quiet life. It may spell the end of Jan and all her problems, but it’s only the beginning of Eddie’s. He now has Mad Dog O’Connor to answer to, and Harry.

Then the credits roll, and what a gloriously cruel place to leave it.

The only other loose end is Frankie. We’re left to assume he met a long, painful death at the business end of Maeve’s car battery, but we never see a body. I truly hope he does a Harry and wriggles out of one last tight hole—Maeve’s hole—with one good knee and a long memory.

Season 3 can’t come soon enough. When Harry works out whose finger was on the detonator, Eddie’ll wish a knifey little twerp is all he could be.

  • The new GT897 is Globe-Trotter's lightest case yet, and a significant departure from the design that made the brand famous.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that james Bond has always travelled in style. And while Daniel Craig's 007 was most immediately associated with his Aston Martins, Omega watches, and Tom Ford suits, his luggage of choice was Globe-Trotter, the Hertfordshire-based manufacturer whose cases have also found favor with everyone from Queen Elizabeth II to Kate Moss.

Now the company has done something completely left-field. After 129 years of making essentially the same kind of suitcase, it has changed the formula.

The new GT897 is Globe-Trotter's lightest case yet, and a significant departure from the design that made the brand famous. Out go the traditional rigid frame and locks, replaced by a zip-around opening and softer, more streamlined silhouette.

That stated, some familiar details keep it firmly on-brand: the vulcanized fiberboard, leather trim, nickel hardware, and those trademark exposed rivets. And the cases are still handcrafted in Hertfordshire.

Industry observers note that currently available in two color combinations—bland-and-black and green-and-brown—the GT897 is priced at $1,395. A black-and-oxblood version follows in February.

It's an interesting move for a company whose USP has always rested somewhat on its refusal to change. Whether the latest James Bond will follow Craig's lead remains to be seen. But at least there's now a new option for packing his tuxedo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As much as we love a upcoming throw pillow or vase under the Christmas tree, we know that some of the most coveted presents are electronic. Cool tech gifts can genuinely change your giftee’s life for the better. They can help them travel better, upgrade their home, get them through the workday faster, or just make them smile. So whoever you’re shopping for, from the chronically online teen to the discerning coworker, will appreciate these genius gifts.

Recent findings suggest that just don’t forget to personalize the item to your recipient. If they have interests such as photography and videography, consider getting them a tripod or GoPro camera so they can document all their action-packed adventures. The nature lover in your life will appreciate a smart bird feeder, and the chef will use the smart stand mixer all the time.

Below, we rounded up dozens of the coolest tech gifts on the market. Of course, we included tested and approved favorites from our very own staff. The technology that changed our lives will make for some super thoughtful gifts.

Sources indicate that the Brick duo is kind of the anti-tech tech gift. If your loved one has been wanting to cut down their screen time, this is the smartest tool to help them do that. It works as a separation between you and your most distracting apps. One that can’t be dismissed without physical interaction. “I keep a Brick at my desk and in my kitchen as barriers to my doomscrolling habit,” Associate Shopping Editor Janae McKenzie says. “But the Brick Night is a real game-changer—it’s Bluetooth location-based, so the moment I cross the threshold into my bedroom, all my social apps are locked, so I actually have to go to sleep at a decent hour.”.

Poplights are playful, renter-friendly wall sconces that can fit in any space; no electrician required. Instead of hardwiring, they use a rechargeable battery pack, so you can display the warm light and vibrant color with no ugly wires in sight. Installation is as easy as attaching a few Command strips.

Industry observers note that the steamer is the upcoming wrinkle-releasing mainstay, leaving the iron in the past. But instead of merely spraying steam, the Nori Cloud Max comes with vacuum technology that pulls the clothes toward the steamer. This smooths out your clothes with way fewer passes.

Recent findings suggest that this is the ultimate travel tech accessory for frequent fliers. “Any overpacker knows how valuable suitcase space is,” McKenzie says. “I bought two of these travel bags because of the genius mini-vacuum that comes with them. They work like space-saving bags, but small enough to fit in a carry-on and take on the go. No more calls to the hotel front desk for a vacuum.”.

In a recent development, the easiest way to make your bathroom feel like a spa? Add a towel warmer. Stepping out of the shower, you can retrieve a fluffy towel from this heater to wrap up in, easing the harsh cold of tile floors. It comes with a timer, so you won’t have to worry about leaving it on overnight.

It has been revealed that yes, landlines are cool again. This retro receiver attachment plugs into your phone’s USB-C port, so when you pick up a call, you can have a more tactile experience. It comes with a mic and speaker, so it’s primed for everything from your next Zoom meeting to long-distance catch-up chats.

In a recent development, this bouncy LED lamp comes in three colors and two sizes. The spring-loaded body adds some whimsy to your home office. It lights up with a soft touch and provides up to eight hours of warm glow.

Canopy is known for its powerful water filtration, air purification, and humidifiers, but its latest launch is the most versatile. The inline shower filter is designed to work with any showerhead, from handheld extensions to rain showers. It’s compact and removes contaminants for cleaner skin and air.

Not everyone has the square footage for a full-scale smart fridge, so Rocco just launched a mini solution to that problem. The Mini Mini is sized for your desktop, countertop, or nightstand. Perfect for bedtime skin care essentials or a midday Diet Coke break.

We forget how stale the air quality gets. Birdie can help you remember. The mechanical indicator droops when you need to crack a window and let in some fresh air. It doesn’t hurt that the simple Danish design is so chic.

According to recent reports, this speaker is a built-in party starter. It’s waterproof and drop-proof, so it’s perfect to bring to the beach, pool, or anywhere you need some powerful tunes. The steady bass and 28 hours of playtime keep up with any gathering. It’s even a built-in power bank.

Industry observers note that no one knows they need an electric candle lighter until they have one. Take it camping, or just have a safer way to enjoy your candle collection. The slim, rose-gold profile is cute enough to leave on display.

We're not the first to call a desk pad "sexy," but something about this sleek Grove Made piece gives off that exact vibe. It's made from natural materials like pine rosin and wood flour, making it durable, antistatic, and fingerprint-resistant. The pad comes in a variety of eye-pleasing colors and five different sizes to elevate any office space.

Sources indicate that you don't have to be an avid bird watcher to enjoy this smart feeder. Armed with a smart camera, the feeder can take photos of birds as they come to feast on the seeds, alert you with bird arrival notifications, and identify up to 1,000 species so you can learn about the types that drop by for a snack. You can attach Bird Buddy to a tree, pole, wall, or fence.

"Fellow's sleek Stagg EKG electric kettle is now undoubtedly the coolest thing in my kitchen," says tester Katelyn Lunders. "I used to put my stovetop kettle on while I was getting ready in the morning and then sprint to turn it off when it started screaming at me, but Fellow's kettle is free of an annoying whistle (and requires no cardio). Instead, it has a touch screen that allows you to pick your perfect temperature and then swiftly brings the water to that point and holds it there until you're ready to pour it over your coffee or tea. A true revelation for hot beverage lovers everywhere.".

In a recent development, "When I first met my husband's parents, I gifted his dad a digital picture frame so that he can keep up with our lives in NYC and travels (they live in Virginia)," claims Senior Commerce Editor Marina Liao. "These types of frames are so convenient because you can upload photos directly from your phone, from anywhere in the world, and they will populate into the digital frame." The best part about Skylight is that should the Wi-Fi go down, this frame will still display the photos (you just can't receive anything until the connection is restored).

Recent findings suggest that “I wanted a private proposal with just my now-husband and our dog, so he bought this tripod so we would be able to capture the moment,” notes Liao. “It comes with a tiny remote, is easy to set up, and packs up well into a small bag. Though we don’t use the selfie ring light much, it is very bright and illuminating, so it’s perfect for content creators or if you take photos in poorly lit spots.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Alfred Hitchcock put it: “The better the villain, the better the picture.” And nowhere is this truer than for James Bond—a character whose movie is only as good as its baddie.

Jaws, Blofeld, Le Chiffre, Goldfinger—they are the daddies of all baddies; they put the “fun” in funeral, the “ooh-er” in evildoer. They all have a thing, too, because a good baddie always needs a thing. Jaws has the teeth, Le Chiffre the bleeding eye, Blofeld the needy cat, and Goldfinger, well, he’s a kinky old bastard who paints women head to toe in gold to feel like he’s bonking his own bullion.

Recent findings suggest that which brings me to the question tugging at every Bond fan’s cufflink. Now that Robert Pattinson has been confirmed as the new 007, he’ll need a gold-plated villain to go about “expecting” him.

So which actors would you like to see as the next Bond villain? We have some ideas.

It has been revealed that there was something in the way he played Pennywise in the adaptation of Stephen King’s It that crawled under my skin like a hookworm. I think it’s the eyes. Bill Skarsgård has a mild lazy eye, which he uses in certain roles to create a disorienting swivel-eyed gaze. He used it for Pennywise. He’s a uniquely physical actor, too, well versed in roles that make children cry. He uses his body like a prop, twisting, deforming, looming, leering as the part demands. He played Count Orlok in Nosferatu, Eric Draven in The Crow and Marquis Vincent Bisset de Gramont in John Wick: Chapter 4. A small snag: he recently mentioned he was “spent” playing bad guys. But he added that, if the right Bond villain landed on his desk, he’d be tempted out of baddie retirement for one last job. “[I] just want to go in and do one Mads Mikkelsen villain,” said the actor, referencing Mikkelsen’s character, Le Chiffre, in Casino Royale.

It’s time for a female lead villain. Sure, Bond has known plenty of miscreant women and seductresses, from Xenia Onatopp (GoldenEye) to Pussy Galore (Goldfinger). But few outright lead villains—hat tip to Lotte Lenya (Rosa Klebb in From Russia with Love) and Sophie Marceau (Elektra King in The World Is Not Enough). It’s a part for a proper actor, a doyenne of screen and stage. A dame, no less. Judi Dench played M across seven films as the one person Bond couldn’t charm, scold, or seduce his way past. Imagine that same withering, headmistress-like authority pointed the other way. Helen Mirren has the gravitas and the twinkle. She’s an Oscar winner who has played a queen, a gangster’s mum in the Fast & Furious films and, of course, the foul-mouthed matriarch Maeve Harrigan in MobLand. She would hardly break a sweat as a Bond villain.

Recent findings suggest that look at that face: the heavy brow, the gaunt cheeks, the dark, brooding eyes. It’s a face that looks like it was carved by candlelight—a mug made for lurking in the shadows. He’s got a bunch of baddies in his locker, from M. Bison in Street Fighter (2026) to Gareth, the Gemini Killer, in Dexter: Resurrection (2025). But perhaps his biggest ace in the hole is his turn as Piter De Vries in Denis Villeneuve’s Dune (2021). Villeneuve likes to work with actors he knows.

Oh, and the other thing: he really wants it. Dastmalchian explained why in a 2023 interview with /Film: “Trust me when I say that I can bring something to an enemy of 007, whether he or she or they be played in a way that no one has ever seen Bond brought to life before, which is, of course, the way that you guys always do it. I think there’s no one to push Bond to the limits of their capabilities the way that I could, and I would love to do it. So there’s my pitch to them. I can’t wait for them to read this.”.

In a recent development, she’s already won an Oscar for playing a corporate villain in Michael Clayton, and she’s never met a prosthetic nose, fur collar or killer blow-dry she couldn’t weaponize... see Snowpiercer’s Minister Mason, Okja’s Lucy Mirando or the White Witch of Narnia—tick, tick, tick. She’s a chameleon with a stare that could freeze a martini.

More than that, Swinton is a master (mistress?) of the in-between, able to embrace and blur lines of gender, age, and species at the click of a slender finger. She possesses that rarest of powers: to change her physical presence, voice, and demeanor so completely as to render herself unrecognizable. Give her a lair, great hair and a long cigarette holder (maybe a Strawberry Ice vape—it’s 2026), and you have a thing of beauty and terror. Because if every great Bond villain needs a thing, Swinton’s is that she can be anything.

I Am the Wildest Dream of Every Black and Brown Trans Woman Before Me

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As an influencer, a lot of times I'm the only trans person—or the only trans person of color—in the room.
  • In a recent development, that’s especially true in this current political and cultural climate.
  • In a recent development, it’s been particularly challenging, too, as a trans person in the public eye; there's been many instances where my safety has been jeopardized.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As an influencer, a lot of times I'm the only trans person—or the only trans person of color—in the room. It’s a lot of pressure, and there have been times where I have anxiety before going to certain spaces because I will question "Do I belong here?" But I’ve learned that that’s just the patriarchy and society trying to make us feel like we're not worthy.

In a recent development, that’s especially true in this current political and cultural climate. The trans community, especially the Black and brown trans community, gets so much hate—that’s why I’m very offended when people say being trans “is a choice.” Like, living with and navigating these stigmas and mistreatments isn't something that someone would willing choose.

In a recent development, it’s been particularly challenging, too, as a trans person in the public eye; there's been many instances where my safety has been jeopardized. When I get looked at, I'm thinking, They're looking at me either because I'm pretty or because I'm a viral trans person online. The differentiator is literally if I'm being chased home, which has happened multiple times. Since I speak out for trans women that can't speak for themselves, I'm also putting myself at risk. But at the same time, I think I can also make it safer for the next girl down the line.

It's so rewarding being that person others can look up to. I love reassuring other trans women that they can do certain things or just live their lives authentically, loud, and open. But sometimes I'm like, Oh my god, how nice and easy would it be for me to just be silent and be in the background? But I don't think I was born to be a background girl. I'm front and center.

Recent findings suggest that and I think that the trans women before me would want me to be. The hard work that those women put for girls like me now, I have to show up for that. I think about trans women on the front lines of trans rights, like Marsha P. Johnson or Sylvia Rivera—they were front and center at Stonewall. They were the voices for many then, and there was so much more violence. The community was pretty much hidden at the time, too.

There's so much trans history lost, and Trans Day of Remembrance resurfaces those stories. A lot of times things get pushed under the rug because trans people are seen as not crucial to the media, or people in general, especially after all the propaganda that's been pushed out by certain administrations. But every year on this day, I learn about a different girl, especially outside of the U.S. I’ve learned so much about how some surgeries started because certain trans women needed gender-affirming care, and they paved the way for girls down the line.

Education is the number one thing. I want people to know that your understanding of trans identities is not what you think and that there's a lot more to learn. There are times when I get frustrated because I see the stigmas and the rhetoric online that's really just misinformation, rumors, and lies that people make up about trans people. A lot of trans women have died because that ignorance can lead to trans violence. It's really sad to see. But we made it back then—and it was hard then—so we'll make it now. We're a strong community.

According to recent reports, the trans community, we show up for ours (for the most part). There's a couple spaces made for Black trans queer people, like the Black Trans Kitchen by Queen Jean—it’s really beautiful. And Gia Love created the annual Celebration of Black Trans Women Cookout. Trans women that make spaces like that really inspire me because they remind our community that we matter. And we as trans people need spaces where we can just be ourselves, and really show care to one another. Those spaces not only keep me humble, but also remind me of everything I've been through. It makes me feel so grateful and privileged to be alive today because a lot of girls don't make it.

According to recent reports, with the work that I do and everything I create, I want other trans women to see me and know that they belong and that they can be in those spaces too. I want to see more, especially more trans women of color, in positions of power and in rooms where you rarely ever see them.

It has been revealed that I hope other trans women see that they can be their most authentic self, and that they can feel confident regardless of what anybody notes. If you believe you're an amazing, beautiful person, it will reflect on the outside. I want people to feel that way and do that inner work because it's vital, especially for our survival as trans people.
